title: Quagga Path
summary: Quagga, also written Quogo or Quago, is recorded as an Indian trail or path in western Southampton at Atlanticville, now the East Quogue area. The name was used for a path leading toward Quaquanantuck Neck and the meadows.
history_content: The path crossed the necks in this part of Southampton. Dated town-record references appear in the Historic Timeline with their boundary language and citations.
translation_content:
Quagga, Quogo, and Quago are shortened or altered forms connected with Quaquanantuck. The fuller name is interpreted elsewhere as a cove or estuary where the land or water quakes or trembles.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names should authentically connect to the place and the people who live, work and visit there.”

— Moreton Bay Regional Council, Caboolture West Place Naming Formalisation: Supporting Information (2022), ‘Meanings of recommended place names,’ page 4
preservation_content: Quagga Path preserves a route name within the Quantuck and East Quogue landscape, showing how trails, necks, meadows, and shortened colonial spellings are tied together in local records.
